I am an old woman here in Kigoma, seventy-six years now, and my hands are not what they used to be. This small plot of mine, not even a tenth of a hectare, I plant it with what I have — mixed together as my mother taught me, so if one crop fails another will feed me. I have no money for those shop fertilizers or the sprays, but I put the droppings from my few chickens and goats on the soil, and I save my own seeds from last season like always. My grandchildren help me sometimes when they are not at school, but mostly it is just me walking slowly with my hoe.
